stories.title: Implement STUN NAT type probing in scp-transport
stories.description: Implement STUN binding requests (RFC 8489) in scp-transport to determine NAT type and external address on startup. NAT type classification (full-cone, address-restricted, port-restricted, symmetric) drives reachability tier selection (§10.12.1). STUN probing is performed against known SCP relays that serve as STUN endpoints. The result determines whether hole punching (Tier 2) is viable or bridge fallback (Tier 3) is required. 25-second keepalive maintains NAT mapping for non-symmetric NATs.

stories.title: Implement UPnP/NAT-PMP port mapping in scp-transport
stories.description: Implement UPnP-IGD and NAT-PMP/PCP port mapping as Tier 1 reachability (§10.12.2). On relay startup, the SDK attempts to map the relay's listening port through the router. If successful, the router's external IP and assigned port become the relay's advertised address. Lease renewal at 50% TTL. Mapping loss triggers re-probe and potential tier change. Uses the igd-next crate for UPnP-IGD and natpmp crate for NAT-PMP/PCP.

stories.title: Support ws:// transport for DHT-discovered relays
stories.description: Extend the relay WebSocket transport to accept ws:// (plaintext) connections for relay URLs obtained from DHT-resolved DID documents (§10.12.6). The SDK MUST reject ws:// relay URLs obtained from .well-known/scp or any non-DHT source. MLS provides the confidentiality boundary; TLS on a dumb pipe is defense-in-depth, not the security layer. This enables self-hosted relays behind NAT with no domain to be reachable without requiring TLS certificates.

stories.title: Implement .no_domain() ApplicationNode builder mode
stories.description: Add .no_domain() to ApplicationNodeBuilder (§10.12.8). When set: skip ACME TLS provisioning, probe NAT type via STUN, attempt UPnP (Tier 1), fallback to STUN address (Tier 2), register with bridge (Tier 3), publish DID document with ws:// relay URL, do NOT serve .well-known/scp. Also adds .stun_server() and .bridge_relay() builder methods for override configuration. This is the zero-config deployment path for self-hosted relays behind residential NAT.

stories.title: Implement BRIDGE relay operation for symmetric NAT fallback
stories.description: Implement the BRIDGE operation (§10.12.4) as Tier 3 fallback for symmetric NAT (~15% of home routers). A willing SCP relay acts as a transparent bridge, proxying blobs bidirectionally to the target self-hosted relay. The bridge does NOT inspect, modify, or cache proxied blobs. Bridge relays see the same metadata as any relay (§9.9.1). Any SCP relay MAY offer bridge service via supports_bridge configuration. Phase 3 component.

stories.title: Implement STUN service on SCP relays
stories.description: Any SCP relay MAY serve as a STUN endpoint (§10.12.3). STUN service is lightweight, stateless, and uses a single UDP socket. stories.title: Implement did_routing_id derivation function
stories.description: Implement the did_routing_id derivation (§3.10.2): SHA-256("scp:did:" || did_string). The "scp:did:" domain separator prevents collision with context routing IDs (HMAC-SHA256(identity_key, context_id) per §5.7.1) and broadcast routing IDs (SHA-256(context_id) per §5.14). This is a pure function with no dependencies — the building block for relay-based DID resolution.

stories.title: Implement DID document PUBLISH to SCP relays via RepublishManager
stories.description: Extend RepublishManager to publish DID documents to SCP relays using existing PUBLISH operation (§3.10.5). DID documents are published as standard blobs with routing_id = did_routing_id(did_string) and blob_ttl = 604800 (7 days). Identity owners SHOULD publish to their own relays plus bootstrap relays. RepublishManager schedules relay republishing on a 6-day cycle (1-day margin before TTL expiry). Publishing to both SCP relays and Mainline DHT is a MUST per the anti-segmentation invariant (§3.10.6).

stories.title: Implement DID document QUERY from SCP relays
stories.description: Implement relay-based DID document resolution using existing QUERY operation (§3.10.4). Resolver computes did_routing_id, queries known SCP relays (identity's relays if known, else bootstrap relays), verifies BEP44 signature against the public key encoded in the DID string, and checks seq >= last_known_seq. This is the relay layer of the dual-layer resolution protocol. Cache results per §9.10.7 (24h active, 7d inactive).

stories.title: Implement DidResolver trait with parallel dual-layer resolution
stories.description: Implement the DidResolver trait (§3.10.10) that composes relay QUERY with DhtClient::resolve() for parallel dual-layer resolution. Both layers are queried in parallel via tokio::join! with per-layer 10-second timeouts. Valid means BEP44 signature verifies AND sequence number >= last known cached sequence. When both return valid documents, highest sequence number wins. On a tie, relay is preferred (lower latency). ResolutionSource enum tracks whether the result came from an SCP relay, Mainline DHT, or cache.

stories.title: Implement reachability self-test on startup
stories.description: After obtaining an external address via UPnP (Tier 1, §10.12.2 step 4) or STUN (Tier 2, §10.12.3), the SDK must perform a reachability self-test before publishing the address in the DID document. stories.title: Implement multi-STUN divergence detection for symmetric NAT
stories.description: Symmetric NAT detection requires comparing external addresses from multiple STUN servers (§10.12.9 threat model). If different STUN servers report different external addresses, the NAT is symmetric. Currently NatProber supports multiple endpoints but only uses the first successful response for classification. This story adds divergence detection: query at least 2 STUN servers, compare external addresses, and classify as symmetric if they diverge.

stories.title: Implement protocol-level healing of stale DID documents across resolution layers
stories.description: Per §3.10.7, when both resolution layers return valid documents with different sequence numbers, the resolver SHOULD re-publish the fresher document to the layer that returned the stale one (protocol-level healing). Currently DualLayerResolver picks the highest seq but does not trigger a republish to the stale layer. This story implements the healing mechanism: when the relay returns seq=1 and DHT returns seq=5, the resolver queues a republish of the seq=5 document to the relay layer.
acceptanceCriteria: When relay returns a lower seq than DHT, the DHT document is republished to relay layer
When DHT returns a lower seq than relay, the relay document is republished to DHT layer

Healing is best-effort (failure is logged, not propagated)

actionItems: Add healing trigger in DualLayerResolver when seq numbers diverge

stories.title: Implement BRIDGE_REGISTER authentication with routing ID ownership proof
stories.description: BRIDGE_REGISTER currently accepts any routing_id without authentication (§10.12.4). An attacker can register arbitrary routing IDs and intercept traffic meant for the legitimate self-hosted relay. This story adds signature-based authentication: the BRIDGE_REGISTER message must include an Ed25519 signature proving the sender owns the DID that maps to the claimed routing_id. The bridge relay verifies the signature before accepting the registration.
